name: FDA's AI Credibility Framework
blurb: The seven step, risk based test the FDA proposes for AI models used in drug submissions.
title: FDA's AI Credibility Framework
answer: The FDA proposes that any AI model producing data for a decision on a drug's safety, effectiveness or quality be shown credible for its specific context of use. Its seven steps run from defining the question and context of use, through assessing model risk, to planning, documenting and judging the credibility evidence. Uses in early discovery and pure operational efficiency are outside its scope.

reading.body:
The FDA's test for AI in drug submissions is not whether a model is good, but whether it is credible for one stated context of use.

That distinction drives the whole framework. A model is not approved in general. It is judged against the specific question it answers and the role its output plays in a decision about a drug's safety, effectiveness or quality. Model risk combines how much a decision depends on the model with how serious a wrong decision would be, and the evidence demanded scales with that risk. The seven steps run from defining the question and context of use, through assessing model risk, to planning, documenting and judging the credibility evidence. The FDA said in January 2025 that it had seen more than 500 drug submissions with AI components since 2016, which is the volume that makes a repeatable test necessary rather than optional.

For AI specifically, this puts the burden on documentation and scoping rather than on model architecture. A team cannot settle the question by pointing to benchmark performance. It has to state what the model is for, show that the evidence matches the risk of that use, and keep the record. Uses in early discovery and pure operational efficiency fall outside the framework's scope, so the same model may be regulated in one part of the pipeline and unregulated in another.

The data covers the framework's structure, its risk logic and the submission volume behind it. It does not give the final guidance status, the comment outcome, or how the FDA will apply the test in practice. The draft was issued with comments due April 2025, and nothing here says what changed after that.

sections.body: Run the seven steps for each model before it touches a submission. Model risk combines how much a decision depends on the model and how serious a wrong decision would be, and the evidence asked for scales with it.

developments.text: The FDA issued its draft guidance on AI to support regulatory decision making for drugs and biologics, docket FDA-2024-D-4689, with comments due in April 2025.
Announcing the framework, the FDA said it had seen more than 500 drug submissions with AI components since 2016.
